hook_text: Want to know if a river is healthy? Ask the bugs under its stones.
clip_script: Step into a stream. Hold a net downstream and kick the stones. Look what's wriggling inside. Mayfly nymphs and stonefly nymphs? They need clean, oxygen-rich water, so the river's probably healthy. Only worms, leeches and blood-red fly larvae? The river may be choking on sewage or fertiliser. That's miniSASS, a South African method anyone can use. And remember: a river is only as healthy as its catchment, all the land that drains into it. Farms, towns, mines, wetlands: it all ends up in the water.
visual_style: Close-up of hands lifting stones in a stream; a white tray with tiny creatures labelled with scores; an aerial pull-back showing the river's whole catchment with towns, farms and wetlands.
pacing: Quick and practical, with a big-picture pull-back at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on river health and catchments.
